hook.text: On November second, a Tengrinews journalist sent Almaty Air Initiative five questions about the city's air.

cost.text: AAI's experts answered by hand: three pages, twenty-three sources, and hours of work.

now.text: Now, the same five questions, asked live.

race.text: Taza Copilot searches only AAI's published research and its live sensors, and answers each question in seconds, with the exact quote, the page, and a link.

match.text: And the facts match AAI's own answer: thirty-one point two micrograms in twenty twenty-five, thirty percent worse than the year before.

metric.text: Across forty-four test questions, including fifteen real questions that journalists and colleagues sent to the initiative, every answer came with a source, in a median of three point three seconds.

trust.text: It checks claims from the news, shows both figures when sources disagree, and says so when the research does not cover a question.

live.text: Live data from more than a hundred and fifty sensors: the map, the best time to go out, comparisons with other cities, and schools ranked by the air right now.

everywhere.text: Ask by voice, on Telegram, on WhatsApp, where you can even call Taza, or from a widget on any website.

decisions.text: And any answer becomes a one-page policy brief.

part2.text: The same research can reach every driver and rider in inDrive.

driver.text: Drivers get a morning alert on bad-air days, and a reminder to close the windows in traffic. In a jam, the air inside a car is forty percent more polluted, says AAI's own fleet study.

rider.text: Riders see the air at their pickup point, and drivers find a cleaner spot for a break.

api.text: All from one API call, and the location is never stored.

aai.text: For AAI, it costs about seven dollars a month, needs no developers, and the code is open.

outro.text: Taza Copilot. Ask AAI's research anything.

s_indrive.text: And inside inDrive: air alerts and advice for drivers and riders.
